Nello STEMI la coronarografia cerca la l:
In STEMI, coronary angiography looks for the culprit lesion: a vessel that stops abruptly, with a "stump" appearance, with the downstream territory not opacified (TIMI 0 flow). Here the descending branch of the left coronary artery stops in its mid portion; on the following sequence, with flow restored, a severe stenosis (90-98%) remains at the same site: it is the ruptured plaque on which the thrombus had formed. Treatment is primary angioplasty with stenting of the culprit lesion, as soon as possible.
How to estimate a stenosis: compare the lumen diameter at the narrowest point with that of the healthy segment just upstream, in at least two projections (an eccentric lesion may look mild in only one). Here there are no measurements in mm: the images are converted and uncalibrated, so the estimate is a visual percentage.
Pitfalls: a branch that "disappears" may simply be overlapped by other vessels or foreshortened (change projection); catheter-induced spasm resolves with nitrates; a myocardial bridge narrows only in systole (look at the whole cycle in the cine).
Note on the vessel name: the collection does not state which branch is occluded; the LAD is the most likely reading from the course toward the apex in sequence 3, but it should be confirmed with angulated projections (not provided).
